In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oxidative stress and inflammation are the main factors in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases, and that the Ang II system plays an important role in this process.
the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system is involved in the development and maintenance of hypertension.
the renin angiotensin aldosterone system (RAAS) has a role in both the pathogenesis of and in the treatment of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AngII is a major player in the development and progression of hypertension.
the AngII-induced oxidative stress is a critical component of the pathogenic actions of AngII.
AngII has an acute vasoconstrictive action, but also has a long-term pressor action that is independent of vasoconstriction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxidative stress that AngII induces can be prevented by the ACE inhibitors and AT1 receptor antagonists that block the formation of AngII and its actions, respectively.
AngII is not only a vasoconstrictor but also a pro-oxidative agent, and this pro-oxidative effect is independent of its pressor action.
the oxidative stress caused by AngII may be a more important contributor to the development of hypertension than its acute vasoconstrictive effects.
